11: 
12: # Evidence Publication Boundary Skill
13: 
14: ## Description
15: 
16: Treat every crossing of a trust boundary by evidence — promotion into canonical
17: records, external citation, or public release — as a gated, one-way event:
18: evidence stays verbatim and quarantined, values never cross, everything outbound
19: is classified and deny-list-checked first, and sign-off happens before the
20: crossing because the crossing cannot be undone.
21: 
22: ## When to Activate
23: 
24: - Material derived from captured or audit evidence will be promoted, cited
25:   externally, or published.
26: - An artifact mixes authored content with host-captured or sensitive-source
27:   lineage.
28: - A release decision would be irreversible once made public.
29: 
30: ## When NOT to Activate
31: 
32: - Content is already classified public with no captured-evidence lineage.
33: - The task is a single unvalidated observation with no repeated pattern behind it.
34: - Runtime enforcement is required but unavailable — apply the procedure manually
35:   and state the limitation instead of claiming technical prevention.
36: - The task needs a different specialist or independent review; hand off.
37: 
38: ## Steps
39: 
40: 1. Identify the trust boundary and which side every reader sits on
41:    (internal reviewer, external stakeholder, public).
42: 2. Confirm captured evidence remains verbatim and quarantined; plan pointers,
43:    indexes, or digests — never copies.
44: 3. Author the outbound artifact as a separate layer: method, scope, and outcome
45:    claims; reproduction from injected fixtures, never internal values.
46: 4. Apply placeholder discipline matched to audience trust: placeholder +
47:    location pointer internally; existence + location class externally; file
48:    digests only, publicly.
49: 5. Run the outbound gate per file: assign classification; check against the
50:    secret deny-list; any match — including warning severity — rejects the file,
51:    reporting the pattern category only; log the event without copying content.
52: 6. Obtain explicit human sign-off before the crossing. Spend all reversibility
53:    (scanning, classification, review) before the boundary, never after.
54: 
55: ## Success Criteria
56: 
57: - No matched value exists outside its originating tier.
58: - Captured evidence is byte-identical to before the task.
59: - The gate result is logged for every outbound file before release.
60: - Sign-off is recorded before any irreversible crossing.
61: - Every external factual claim traces to at least one internal artifact via a
62:   pointer, index entry, or digest.
63: 
64: ## Examples
65: 
66: ### Good
67: 
68: A case-study summary states method, scope, and outcome; cites a credential-shaped
69: token as "placeholder near line 12 of an internal record"; publishes digests of
70: the internal evidence set; logs the gate pass; ships only after recorded sign-off.
71: 
72: ### Bad
73: 
74: Quoting "just the example output" from a raw transcript; describing a secret's
75: shape precisely enough to reconstruct it; releasing first and redacting after
76: discovery; skipping classification because "it's obviously fine".
77: 
78: ## Boundaries
79:

# Evidence Publication Boundary Skill

## Description

Treat every crossing of a trust boundary by evidence — promotion into canonical
records, external citation, or public release — as a gated, one-way event:
evidence stays verbatim and quarantined, values never cross, everything outbound
is classified and deny-list-checked first, and sign-off happens before the
crossing because the crossing cannot be undone.

## When to Activate

- Material derived from captured or audit evidence will be promoted, cited
  externally, or published.
- An artifact mixes authored content with host-captured or sensitive-source
  lineage.
- A release decision would be irreversible once made public.

## When NOT to Activate

- Content is already classified public with no captured-evidence lineage.
- The task is a single unvalidated observation with no repeated pattern behind it.
- Runtime enforcement is required but unavailable — apply the procedure manually
  and state the limitation instead of claiming technical prevention.
- The task needs a different specialist or independent review; hand off.

## Steps

1. Identify the trust boundary and which side every reader sits on
   (internal reviewer, external stakeholder, public).
2. Confirm captured evidence remains verbatim and quarantined; plan pointers,
   indexes, or digests — never copies.
3. Author the outbound artifact as a separate layer: method, scope, and outcome
   claims; reproduction from injected fixtures, never internal values.
4. Apply placeholder discipline matched to audience trust: placeholder +
   location pointer internally; existence + location class externally; file
   digests only, publicly.
5. Run the outbound gate per file: assign classification; check against the
   secret deny-list; any match — including warning severity — rejects the file,
   reporting the pattern category only; log the event without copying content.
6. Obtain explicit human sign-off before the crossing. Spend all reversibility
   (scanning, classification, review) before the boundary, never after.

## Success Criteria

- No matched value exists outside its originating tier.
- Captured evidence is byte-identical to before the task.
- The gate result is logged for every outbound file before release.
- Sign-off is recorded before any irreversible crossing.
- Every external factual claim traces to at least one internal artifact via a
  pointer, index entry, or digest.

## Examples

### Good

A case-study summary states method, scope, and outcome; cites a credential-shaped
token as "placeholder near line 12 of an internal record"; publishes digests of
the internal evidence set; logs the gate pass; ships only after recorded sign-off.

### Bad

Quoting "just the example output" from a raw transcript; describing a secret's
shape precisely enough to reconstruct it; releasing first and redacting after
discovery; skipping classification because "it's obviously fine".

## Boundaries

- Procedural only. Whether the gate runs as human discipline or CI/release
  tooling is environment-dependent and must be stated, not assumed.
- Does not authorize automatic promotion to memory or canonical files.
- Does not replace independent security review for high-blast-radius releases.
- Evidence retention/expiry is out of scope (recorded project-level gap).

Treat every crossing of a trust boundary by evidence — promotion into canonical
records, external citation, or public release — as a gated, one-way event:
evidence stays verbatim and quarantined, values never cross, everything outbound

- Material derived from captured or audit evidence will be promoted, cited

- An artifact mixes authored content with host-captured or sensitive-source
  lineage.
- A release decision would be irreversible once made public.

- Content is already classified public with no captured-evidence lineage.
- The task is a single unvalidated observation with no repeated pattern behind it.
